title: Komal Saul Jolpan
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Use curd without gelatin and pure jaggery. Can be made vegan with plant-based milk.
recipe: Soak Komal Saul in warm water for 15–25 minutes until soft (no cooking required).
Drain and mix with curd or milk and jaggery. Add sliced banana if desired.
Serve as a light traditional Assamese breakfast (jolpan).
tips: Unique GI-tagged rice that needs only soaking – a farmer's quick meal.
Part of classic jolpan culture with Assam tea.

title: Til Pitha
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Ensure jaggery is pure and free from animal-based processing agents.
recipe: Dry-roast sesame seeds and grind coarsely with jaggery to make the filling.
Make a thin batter or dough with rice flour and water. Spread thinly on a hot tawa or leaf.
Place filling in the centre, fold or roll, and cook both sides till done.
Serve warm as a festive Bihu breakfast or snack.
tips: Iconic Bihu pitha – crispy outside, sweet sesame-jaggery inside.
Made especially during Magh Bihu.

title: Poita Bhat
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and use only green chilli and salt.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, green chilli, onion, salt
Optional: mashed potato or fried fish

recipe: Soak cooked rice in water overnight to ferment lightly.
In the morning, drain excess water if preferred. Mix with mustard oil, chopped green chilli, onion and salt.
Serve with aloo pitika or any side.
tips: Cooling summer breakfast of rural Assam – probiotic and refreshing.
Simple and zero-waste use of leftover rice.

title: Masor Tenga
jainNotes: Contains fish - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Tomato or ou tenga / thekera / lemon
Mustard oil, turmeric, green chilli, fenugreek or cumin

recipe: Lightly fry fish pieces with turmeric and salt in mustard oil; set aside.
In the same oil temper fenugreek/cumin and green chilli. Add tomato or chosen souring agent and cook till soft.
Add water, salt and the fried fish. Simmer gently till the broth is light, sour and flavourful.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with steamed rice as the closing dish of a meal.
tips: Signature sour fish curry of Assam – light, tangy and minimal spice.
Traditionally ends the meal after khar.

title: Khar (e.g. Raw Papaya or Xaak Khar)
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Raw papaya or mustard greens / any vegetable
Kola khar (banana ash filtrate) or baking soda substitute
Mustard oil, garlic, green chilli, salt

recipe: Prepare or use filtered banana-ash water (kola khar).
Cook the vegetable with a little mustard oil, garlic and green chilli.
Add the khar liquid and simmer till the vegetable is soft and the dish has a distinctive alkaline flavour.
Serve as the traditional opening dish of an Assamese meal with rice.
tips: Unique alkaline starter that defines Assamese thali structure.
Traditionally made from sun-dried banana peel ash.

title: Aloo Pitika
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Mash the boiled potatoes while still warm.
Mix in raw mustard oil, finely chopped onion, green chilli, coriander and salt.
Serve as a side with rice, dal and tenga or khar.
tips: Simple, pungent mash that appears in almost every Assamese thali.
The raw mustard oil is essential for authentic flavour.

title: Pork with Bamboo Shoot (Gahori Kharisa)
jainNotes: Contains pork, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cut pork into pieces. Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, ginger, garlic and chilli.
Add pork and cook till it releases fat and browns lightly.
Add fermented bamboo shoot and salt. Cover and simmer till pork is tender and flavours meld.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Popular among many communities in Assam – the fermented bamboo shoot gives distinctive tang.
Minimal spices allow the pork and khorisa to shine.

title: Assamese Duck Curry (Hanhor Mangxo)
jainNotes: Contains duck, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, turmeric, black pepper, salt

recipe: Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, ginger-garlic and chilli. Add duck pieces and brown well.
Add turmeric, pepper, salt and potato. Add a little water and slow-cook till duck is tender and gravy is rich.
Serve with rice.
tips: Duck is highly prized in Assamese cuisine, especially for festive occasions.
Often cooked with minimal spices to highlight the meat.

title: Kholasapori Pitha (Plain)
jainNotes: Plain version is Jain-compatible (rice flour, water, salt, mustard oil). Avoid vegetable/onion additions.
recipe: Make a pouring batter of rice flour, water and salt.
Heat a pan or tawa with a little mustard oil. Pour and spread the batter into thin circles.
Cook both sides till golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve hot with jaggery or tea.
tips: Also called pani pitha or bhurbhuri pitha – simple everyday rice pancake.
Popular breakfast or tea-time item.

title: Kholasapori Pitha with Vegetables
jainNotes: Contains onion and vegetables - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Make a pouring batter of rice flour, water and salt. Add chopped vegetables and onion.
Heat a pan or tawa with a little mustard oil. Pour and spread the batter into thin circles.
Cook both sides till golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve hot with tea.
tips: Savory version with vegetables – common tea-time snack.
Crispy outside, soft inside.

title: Narikol Laru
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Ensure jaggery is pure and free from animal-based processing agents.
recipe: Cook grated coconut and jaggery together on low heat, stirring continuously, till the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Add cardamom if using. Cool slightly and shape into small balls (laru).
Store in an airtight container.
tips: Classic Assamese sweet for Bihu and everyday tea-time.
Simple two-ingredient delight.

title: Lai Xaak / Mixed Greens Stir-fry
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.

ingredients.name: Lai xaak or mixed local greens
Mustard oil, garlic, green chilli, salt

recipe: Heat mustard oil, add crushed garlic and green chilli.
Add the washed greens and salt. Stir-fry on high heat till wilted but still bright.
Serve as a dry side with rice.
tips: Everyday green side dish – Assam has a huge variety of xaak (leafy greens).
Minimal oil and quick cooking preserve nutrients and flavour.

title: Ou Tenga with Fish
jainNotes: Contains fish - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, turmeric, green chilli, salt

recipe: Cut ou tenga into pieces. Lightly fry fish with turmeric and salt.
Temper mustard oil with green chilli, add ou tenga and turmeric. Cook till soft.
Add fish, water and salt. Simmer into a light sour curry.
Serve with rice.
tips: Ou tenga is a classic local souring agent for tenga dishes.
Gives a unique fruity sourness distinct from tomato or lemon.

title: Ou Tenga with Vegetables
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, turmeric, green chilli, salt

recipe: Cut ou tenga into pieces. Heat mustard oil, add green chilli and vegetables.
Add ou tenga, turmeric and salt. Cook till vegetables are soft.
Add water and simmer into a light sour vegetable curry.
Serve with rice.
tips: Vegetarian version of the classic sour curry.
Ou tenga gives a unique fruity sourness distinct from tomato or lemon.
